title: Equivalences into a vertex are the final objects of its join slice
statement: Use quasicategories, equivalence edges, right-pinched mapping spaces, Kan complexes and weak contractibility as in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Let $\mathcal C$ be a quasicategory, let $x,t$ be vertices, and let $f:x\to t$ be an edge. Regard $f$ as a vertex of the join slice $\mathcal C_{/t}$ defined in [lem-coef-infinity-slice-right-fibration]. Then $f$ is an equivalence edge in $\mathcal C$ if and only if for every vertex $a\in\mathcal C_{/t}$ the right-pinched mapping space $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C_{/t}}(a,f)$ is a weakly contractible Kan complex. Equivalently, the equivalence arrows with target $t$ are precisely the final objects of this slice; this does not assume that $t$ itself is final in $\mathcal C$.

source.place: Proposition 4.7.3.20 (02J2), equivalence (1) and (2). Proposition 4.6.5.10 (01L5) identifies the unpinched mapping spaces in the final-object definition with the right-pinched spaces used here, and Proposition 4.6.5.5 (01L0) supplies their Kan property. These are Kerodon tags, not Stacks tags. Online source read; archival copy WANTED in report.md.

proof.text:
Put $E=\mathcal C_{/t}$. The join-slice theorem [lem-coef-infinity-slice-right-fibration] makes $E$ a quasicategory. For $K=\Delta^0$, its degree-$n$ definition is precisely maps $\Delta^{n+1}\to\mathcal C$ with last vertex $t$, with operators extending $\alpha$ by the last vertex. Thus $E$ is the simplicial set $S_t$ of [lem-coef-infinity-slice-arrow-equivalence]. That node supplies an equivalence
$$\delta:E\longrightarrow T=\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,\mathcal C)\times_{\operatorname{ev}_1,\mathcal C}\{t\}.$$
In degree zero $\rho_0:\Delta^0\times\Delta^1\to\Delta^1$ is the identity under the canonical identification, so $\delta$ sends the vertex $f$ to the same arrow $f$ in $T$. Both $E,T$ are quasicategories. Their right-pinched mapping spaces are Kan by [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus], applied to each category and the shape $\Delta^0$, whose functor category is the category itself.

source.place: Slice diagonal equivalence; explicit degree-zero formula and the Kan mapping-space assertion of the cited nodes

proof.text: We first record the elementary consequence of [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition] that precomposition or postcomposition with an equivalence edge is a homotopy equivalence on mapping spaces. If $u$ has inverse class represented by $v$, the composites of the two induced maps are composition with $[v][u]=[\mathrm{id}]$ and $[u][v]=[\mathrm{id}]$. Associativity, unitality and dependence only on the component class, all stated in that node, identify these composites with identity homotopy classes. This also shows that replacing either endpoint by an equivalent object preserves weak contractibility of a mapping space: the two maps induce mutually inverse maps on components and on all homotopy groups (with basepoints transported along the inverse homotopies).

Finality of $f$ in $E$ is equivalent to finality of $\delta(f)$ in $T$. Here are both directions, rather than treating finality as automatic under an equivalence. By [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus], $\delta$ induces weak equivalences on every mapping space. If $\delta(f)$ is final, apply this to each pair $(a,f)$ to see that $\operatorname{Map}_E(a,f)$ is weakly contractible. Conversely, take a quasi-inverse $L$ and a coherent natural equivalence $\delta L\simeq\mathrm{id}_T$, as in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Its component $\epsilon_b:\delta L(b)\to b$ is an equivalence by the componentwise assertion of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus], with shape $T$. The universes can be enlarged so this shape is small. Step 2 gives an equivalence from $\operatorname{Map}_T(b,\delta f)$ to $\operatorname{Map}_T(\delta L(b),\delta f)$, while the latter is weakly equivalent to $\operatorname{Map}_E(L(b),f)$. If $f$ is final in $E$ this last space is weakly contractible. Thus every incoming mapping space to $\delta f$ is weakly contractible, proving the converse. Terminal and final both denote the mapping-space condition of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones].

source.place: Transport along the slice diagonal, expanded using mapping spaces, a quasi-inverse and composition

proof.text:
Now apply [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] with ambient category $\mathcal C$, shape $K=\Delta^0$, and diagram the vertex $t$. The map $\mathcal C\to\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^0,\mathcal C)$ and its evaluation inverse are degreewise identities under $\Delta^0\times\Delta^n\cong\Delta^n$. Consequently the coherent cone category in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones] is exactly $T$: a cone with apex $z$ is an edge $z\to t$, and the cone $\mu$ with apex $x$ is the specified edge $f$. The cited cone-calculus node says that $\mu$ is limiting, hence terminal in $T$, if and only if for every vertex $z$ the postcomposition map
$$P_z:\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(z,x)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(z,t),\qquad h\longmapsto f\circ h,$$
is an equivalence of spaces. The composition here is the canonical class of [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition], characterized there by restrictions from fixed-vertex $2$-simplex strings and the specified pinch inclusions. Thus it is the postcomposition used in the cited cone criterion, rather than an arbitrary operation agreeing only on components. Changing the representing simplicial map does not change whether it is a weak equivalence.

source.place: The explicitly stated general cone criterion, specialized to the singleton shape. This is an existing agent-formulated foundation; Kerodon 02R3 is only its coslice analogue, not a source asserting the general comma criterion.

proof.text: If $f$ is an equivalence, choose an inverse edge $g:t\to x$ as in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Step 2, using [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition], gives that each $P_z$ has inverse up to homotopy given by postcomposition with $g$. Thus Step 4 makes $f$ final in $T$, and Step 3 makes it final in $E$. Its incoming mapping spaces are already Kan by Step 1, so they satisfy the exact right-pinched weak-contractibility condition of the item.

source.place: Two inverse composition operations, followed by Steps 3 and 4

proof.text:
Conversely suppose all $\operatorname{Map}_E(a,f)$ are weakly contractible. By Steps 3 and 4, every $P_z$ induces a bijection on components. For $z=t$, surjectivity gives an edge $g:t\to x$ whose component satisfies $[f][g]=[\mathrm{id}_t]$. For $z=x$, compute, using [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition],
$$\pi_0(P_x)([g][f])=[f][g][f]=[f]=\pi_0(P_x)([\mathrm{id}_x]).$$
Injectivity gives $[g][f]=[\mathrm{id}_x]$. Thus $[g]$ is a two-sided inverse to $[f]$; the equivalence criterion in that composition node gives that $f$ is an equivalence edge. This proves the reverse implication with the stated witnesses. Neither direction used finality of $t$ in $\mathcal C$.
